title: Oracle, Gears, or Data?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Twelve prediction cards, from Delphi's oracle, the Antikythera mechanism, Babylonian eclipse tablets, a stone peg calendar, and modern phones and apps; the learner drags or assigns each card to one of three bins, Oracle, Cycle model, or Learned model, then checks all twelve with card-level feedback on how each answer was produced.

educational.subjectArea: History of Science and Computer Science
educational.topic: Three ways of predicting: the oracle, the cycle model, and the learned model
learningObjectives: Differentiate twelve predictions by how each answer is produced, as an oracle's answer, a cycle model, or a learned model, sorting at least 10 of the 12 correctly on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Machine learning and the predictive model

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Differentiation sorting into three method bins with a single scored first Check, card-level feedback, and unlimited practice re-checks
keyQuestions: Why do a bronze dial, a clay tablet, and a stone calendar share a bin?
What can a learned model do that the Antikythera gears could not?
commonMisconceptions: Anything ancient is guesswork or religion, so the mechanism and the Babylonian tables belong with the oracle.
Any machine that predicts must have learned from data, so the mechanism belongs with the learned models.
The bin depends on the material, clay, stone, bronze or software, rather than on the method that produced the answer.
assessmentOpportunities: First-Check score on twelve cards (mastery: 10 of 12).
Classify a new prediction, such as a weather app, and justify the bin by its method.
